content:
maria-support: Customer (acme-inc) reporting intermittent 502/504 on long-lived streaming requests to eu1. Started ~15:23 UTC after we began a canary model swap. ~10% failure rate, fails after ~25-30s. Escalating :warning:
triage-bot: INCIDENT SUP-8742 created, priority P1, paging oncall.
nina-cs: Affected accounts: acme-inc-prod and acme-lite. Customer says batch job hit ~40 failures in the morning window.
maria-support: Here's a minimal repro curl they ran (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Request-ID: req-01a23" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --no-buffer -d '{"stream": true, "model": "gpt-large-v2"}' https://api.eu1.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```
maria-support: Path returns streaming tokens for ~20s then HTTP/1.1 502 or sometimes 504. Customer attached traces: req-01a23, req-01a24.
devon-sre: Can you paste the exact X-Request-IDs and timestamps? I want to grep Envoy upstream_reset and 5xx counters in logs.
maria-support: ids above. Sample timestamps: 2026-03-17T15:23:12Z and 2026-03-17T15:24:01Z.
alex-obs: Observability: spike in envoy.upstream_rq_5xx at 15:23:12 UTC across frontdoor-eu1. upstream_reset_reason shows "connection termination by peer" for many streams. CPU on model shard-7 jumped at same time.
liang-eng-runtime: We started canary deploy ~15:20 UTC rolling 10% traffic to new model bundle (gpt-large-v2-canary). That model warms up KV cache with several heavy I/O ops at startup — might be causing backend worker stalls and connection closes.
devon-sre: Likely symptom: backend closing connection mid-stream (envoy reports downstream reset -> 502). Two immediate mitigations: rollback canary OR change routing to exclude streaming route from canary. Which is feasible quicker?
liang-eng-runtime: Rollback is fastest. Patch to routing will take longer (needs console + infra approval).
maria-support: Customer requests a workaround they can apply while we fix: pin to model version or split workload to non-streaming endpoints.
liang-eng-runtime: Rollback command (internal): `kubectl -n runtime set image deployment/model-server model-server=redwood/model:stable-2026-02-20` — will revert canary binary.
triage-bot: Support ticket SUP-8742 updated: assigned -> devon-sre, runtime oncall paged.
devon-sre: Also checking Envoy config: frontdoor idle_timeout is 30s. If backend stalls > idle_timeout we get 504. Increasing idle_timeout to 45s is a temporary mitigation but touches global config. Prefer rollback.
alex-obs: Correlated logs: backend process pid=4321 wrote "fatal: worker closed connection during write" around the same times. Stack traces point to blocking disk read in model startup path.
nina-cs: I'll tell customer we're rolling back canary and give them pinning steps. Also ask for their preferred maintenance window if a longer rollback needed.
maria-support: Providing customer repro + workaround. Will confirm after rollback. Thanks. :thumbsup:
devon-sre: Rolling back now, ETA ~3m. Will follow up with patch notes and metrics post-rollback.
liang-eng-runtime: After rollback, we should add a canary gating check that prevents streaming traffic to nodes with cold KV warmup. Filing a follow-up RFC.
triage-bot: SUP-8742 status -> remediation in progress.
devon-sre: Update: rollback completed at 2026-03-17T15:27:10Z. Monitoring 5xx counters.
alex-obs: Post-rollback: envoy.upstream_rq_5xx dropped to baseline within 60s. No new resets for tracked IDs.
maria-support: Customer notified, they report successful runs with no failures in the next batch. Closing escalation once they confirm 24h.
liang-eng-runtime: Follow-up action items: (1) Add streaming-safe canary gating, (2) instrument KV warmup duration + shed streaming, (3) run soak test for model startup.
triage-bot: SUP-8742 -> assigned actions to eng-runtime and dev-sre.
